```typescript
// samples/capybara.ts
// This module defines a basic capybara interface and a sample implementation.
// It serves as a test case for type checking and basic functionality.

interface Capybara {
  name: string;
  isHappy: boolean;
  sayHello(): string;
}

class FriendlyCapybara implements Capybara {
  name: string;
  isHappy: boolean;

  constructor(name: string) {
    this.name = name;
    this.isHappy = true;
  }

  sayHello(): string {
    return `Hello, I am ${this.name}!`;
  }
}

// Example usage and export
const capy = new FriendlyCapybara("Capy-chan");
console.log(capy.sayHello());

export { Capybara, FriendlyCapybara };
```

The initial goal is a simple, type-safe TypeScript module. First, a `Capybara` interface is defined. Then, a class `FriendlyCapybara` that implements the interface is created. The class provides a constructor and `sayHello` method. Finally, an instance of the class is created and its method called, for demonstration purposes. This module is exported for use elsewhere.
